intent: Close the clean-host oracle custody deadlock. Prepare the exact persistent oracle roots after static identities exist, create volatile roots through no-follow directory descriptors, apply exact ownership and modes with fchown/fchmod despite systemd UMask, and reject hostile pre-existing links or foreign custody without widening the oracle unit namespace. Preserve the held-out evaluator boundary and root-only receipt membrane.

gates.name: oracle-release-ruff
gates.command: python -m ruff check scripts/runtime/sadhana_oracle_sandbox.py scripts/runtime/sadhana_release.py tests/test_sadhana_oracle_sandbox.py tests/test_sadhana_release.py

negative_controls.name: oracle-custody-hostiles
negative_controls.command: python -m pytest -q tests/test_sadhana_oracle_sandbox.py tests/test_sadhana_release.py -k 'oracle and (symlink or custody or mode or umask or clean_host)'

commit.message: fix(ops): prepare oracle custody on clean hosts

interface_mismatches: systemd ReadWritePaths are namespace admission, not directory creation; every non-optional persistent path must exist before the oracle-directory oneshot enters its sandbox.
mkdir(mode) is filtered by UMask and does not establish ownership. Exact oracle custody requires descriptor-bound fchown/fchmod before validation.
A hostile pre-existing link or foreign directory must be rejected, not repaired by following or silently taking custody.
honest_blockers: Local tests cannot prove the rendered unit enters its namespace on Ubuntu systemd 255; live systemd-analyze verification and a clean-host predispatch canary remain required.
This packet creates custody roots only. It does not execute the held-out evaluator, authorize provider dispatch, publish a Tailscale route, or weaken evaluator/input/verdict separation.
Concurrent release-controller work also touches sadhana_release.py and its tests; final integration must replay this scoped diff onto the release worker's verified head and rerun all combined gates.
session_entry.rollback: Stop dispatch and the oracle path/timer/service units, retain all oracle inputs, claims, runs, quarantine entries, terminals, and receipts for forensics, and revert only the clean-host custody preparation code. Never delete or relax a hostile path to make rollback pass.
